processing_steps.method: induction melting and casting to round bars
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The material was melted in an induction furnace under Ar atmosphere and cast to round bars, 25 mm in diameter.
Hot-rolled to 75% thickness reduction at 1100 °C and water quenched.
Hot-rolled material solution-treated for 2 h at 1100 °C under Ar and finally quenched in water; this is the parent process of the short annealing treatment.

Short annealing treatment (450 °C/1 h) applied to both the 2Al and 8Al steels; subsequent annealing treatments were performed between 450 and 650 °C. This is the defining process of the current sample (state labelled 450 °C/1 h).

structures.overall_structure: The short annealed 2Al steel (450 °C/1 h) is in the solid solution state consisting of austenite (γ phase); its grain interior remains essentially single-phase austenite with no intergranular carbides (those appear only after long annealing).

Upon tensile deformation the short annealed 2Al steel develops a multiple-stage strain-hardening microstructure: planar dislocation configurations (Taylor lattice structures and highly dense dislocation walls) which, at high stress (true stress of 950 MPa), are transformed by frequent cross-slip into wavy dislocation structures such as dislocation cells and cell blocks; at high stress levels deformation twinning is activated, producing twin bundles (the second, twinning-induced plasticity hardening stage).
structures.microstructure_counts: Dislocation cell block average size of 270 ± 70 nm at a true stress of 950 MPa

defects.type: planar dislocation configurations (Taylor lattice structures and highly dense dislocation walls) that, at high stress (true stress of 950 MPa), transform via cross-slip into wavy dislocation structures (dislocation cells and cell blocks)
deformation twinning (twin bundles containing several deformation twins), activated at high stress levels as the second strain-hardening stage (twinning-induced plasticity)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical tensile specimens, gauge 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: In addition to tensile testing to failure, interrupted tensile tests to different strain levels were performed to study the microstructural evolution as a function of strain.

strain_hardening_rate.value: plateau near 1.9–2.0 GPa between ~1100 and 1600 MPa true stress (second hardening stage)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Within the 2Al steel, the short annealed state (this sample, obtained by 450 °C/1 h) and the long annealed state (650 °C/72 h) exhibit nearly identical yield stress (short annealing YS = 420 MPa vs long annealing YS = 400 MPa), while the long annealing mainly causes a significant reduction in uniform elongation (short annealing UE = 75% vs long annealing UE = 35%); both annealing states exhibit identical flow behavior with only a slight variation in yield stress.

characterization_methods.technique: uniaxial tensile testing (including interrupted tensile tests to different strain levels)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 5 × 10^-4 s^-1; cylindrical specimens with gauge 6 mm diameter and 40 mm length; sections examined were longitudinal (observation direction perpendicular to the tensile axis)
characterization_methods.purpose: to determine engineering stress–strain curves and mechanical properties (YS, UTS, UE) and to study the microstructural evolution as a function of strain
characterization_methods.key_findings: Short annealed 2Al steel: YS = 420 MPa, UTS = 935 MPa, UE = 75%.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Crossbeam instrument (XB 1540, Carl Zeiss SMT AG, Germany), using a recently developed EBSD-based set-up to obtain ECCI images under controlled diffraction conditions
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: longitudinal sections (observation direction perpendicular to the tensile axis)
characterization_methods.purpose: to characterize dislocation and interface contrast / the deformation structures of the tensile-deformed high-Mn steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: The short annealed 2Al steel develops planar dislocation configurations similar to Taylor-lattice structures and HDDWs; at high stress the structure refines to wavy dislocation cells/cell blocks.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Phillips CM20 microscope; thin foils prepared by electropolishing using 30% nitric acid in methanol at −30 °C and 10 V
characterization_methods.purpose: to characterize the deformation structures and precipitation state
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the solid-solution short annealed 2Al steel no nanosized shearable precipitates control hardening; strain hardening is governed by dislocation and twin substructures.

analytical_models.model_name: Dislocation substructure contribution to flow stress
analytical_models.equation_role: Describes the contribution of the dislocation substructure (Taylor lattice structures, dislocation cells and cell blocks) to the flow stress of the short annealed 2Al steel (first hardening stage).
analytical_models.model_note: Δσ = G M K b / D (Eq. 1); G shear modulus, K a constant, b the magnitude of the Burgers vector, M the Taylor factor and D the size of the corresponding dislocation substructure.

analytical_models.equation_role: Describes the contribution of deformation twinning to hardening (second, twinning-induced plasticity hardening stage) of the short annealed 2Al steel.
analytical_models.model_note: Δσ_twinning = K_H-P / (λ_twin)^(1/2) (Eq. 2); K_H-P is a constant and λ_twin the average twin spacing.

unmapped_findings: Estimated twinning stress for the 2Al steel: σ_twinning ~ γ/b = 670–750 MPa, assuming γ = 60 mJ m^-2, b = 0.25 nm and a Taylor factor of 2.8–3.2 (the estimate is stated within the long-annealed 2Al discussion but the parameters are general to the 2Al steel; its attribution to this specific short-annealed sample is therefore not fully certain).

The high carbon content (1.2 wt.%) plays a significant role in the formation of the dislocation substructure of the (low-Al) 2Al steel, ascribed to the role of solute carbon in dislocation cross-slip.

The stress–strain curves of the annealed 2Al steels exhibit a pronounced variation in slope at about 15% strain, where the slope decreases but remains positive, indicating the activation of a secondary strain hardening stage and multiple-strain-hardening behavior for the short annealed 2Al steel.

The outstanding strength–elongation balance of the short annealed 2Al alloy (UTS: 935 MPa; UE: 75%) is attributed to its multiple-stage strain hardening behavior, associated with dislocation substructure refinement and subsequent activation of deformation twinning at high stress levels.

In the short annealed 8Al steel (a different sample/alloy), planar dislocation substructures remain stable up to high stress levels (true stress of 1.1 GPa); this finding pertains to the 8Al steel and is recorded here only to avoid mis-assigning it to the 2Al sample.
